fieldMarks: 10-12 in; blue-gray quail with a fluffy white crest (hence 'cottontop').
Dark edges on gray body feathers create a scaled look.
Sexes very similar; female may have a shorter crest.
behavior: Coveys travel on foot and tend to run rather than fly when disturbed.
Males call from fence posts or rocks in spring; coveys roost on the ground in dense low growth at night.
Eats weed and woody-plant seeds (snakeweed, Russian thistle, mesquite), green leaves and berries, and more insects than most quail.
habitat: Flat open country or rolling hills with grasses, annual weeds and scattered shrubs; also grassland grading into desert, juniper slopes and dry brush.
range: Permanent resident of the arid southwestern United States: the southern Plains, southern Rockies, Southwest and Texas.
